lucy: Hey team, customer reported embeddings API throwing intermittent 400s and big tail latency spikes on /v1/embeddings. Happens when they send a mix of very small single-item requests and occasional large batched requests. Error: "Dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768" for some requests. Also seeing p99 go from ~120ms to 2.5s during the window. Anyone seen this pattern with dynamic batching + max_batch_size?

samir: Thanks for flagging. Can you paste a minimal repro (payload + timestamps) and confirm model route + max_batch_size? Also which deployment (hosted/dedicated/private)?

lucy: Repro sketch below, customer is on hosted API, route is "embeddings/text-embedding-002" pinned. Their SDK is sending single-item requests continuously, then every few minutes a job sends a 40-item batch. Their account has max_batch_size=64 (default). Sample payloads:

```json
# small request (single)
{
  "input": "short text",
  "model": "text-embedding-002"
}

# large job (batch of 40)
{
  "input": ["...", "..." /* 40 items */],
  "model": "text-embedding-002"
}
```

When the large job hits while many singles are queued, we see slow draining and the dimension errors pop up (we suspect stateful coalescing or variant selection issue).

kevin: Curious — dimension mismatch suggests some payload got routed to a different variant/route (maybe a 768-dim model) or the coalesced batch got partially truncated. Two possibilities: 1) mixed-model routing (fallback) or 2) dynamic batching slot assignment when slabbing small+large requests. Can you share an example request id and a server log snippet?

lucy: Got one request id: rq_8f2b9c. Log around the error: 

```
2026-03-16T14:12:03.123Z ERROR batcher: request=rq_8f2b9c coalesce_size=41 max_batch=64 route=embeddings/text-embedding-002 variant=quant-1536
2026-03-16T14:12:03.124Z ERROR runtime: dimension check failed expected=1536 actual=768 payload_idx=22 request_id=rq_8f2b9c
2026-03-16T14:12:03.125Z WARN batcher: dropped 1 reqs, reason=dim-check-fail
```

kevin: That variant name looks like it should be 1536 but the runtime got 768 — possible double-quantized variant or an older model binary on a shard. Two quick checks: 1) confirm model fingerprint for that variant across serving nodes `redwoodctl models list --route embeddings/text-embedding-002 --verbose` 2) check batch composition histograms around that timestamp: `metrics.query("batch_size_histogram", start=... end=...)`.

maya: Also check batching params on the route (coalesce_window_ms, adaptive_slotting). If coalesce_window_ms is long, single requests will wait and be packed with the big job, which increases tail latency. If adaptive_slotting is off, large jobs can monopolize slots. For immediate mitigation I recommend: set max_batch_size=32 for that route and enable adaptive_slotting=true. Optionally set coalesce_window_ms=10 to reduce head-of-line aggregation.

lucy: Trying suggested mitigations now on a canary config for that customer (route-level override). Will update.

infra-bot: Trace created: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/rq_8f2b9c (internal link) :robot_face:

samir: If you're running the canary, please also collect the following for the same timeframe: p50/p95/p99 token latency, batch queue length, per-shard variant hash, and the `coalesce_count` metric. Those will help confirm whether the mismatch is routing vs. packing bug.

lucy: Canary applied at 14:18 UTC: max_batch_size=32, adaptive_slotting=true, coalesce_window_ms=10. Early signs: p99 dropped to ~220ms for ~5m, customer says 400s error rate dropped to 0. But I still see one dim-check failure at 14:24 (maybe in-flight node). Full log:

```
2026-03-16T14:24:12.987Z ERROR runtime: dimension check failed expected=1536 actual=768 request_id=rq_8f2b9c-2 node=svc-embed-07
```

kevin: That node indicates a stale binary or mislabelled variant on svc-embed-07 — please flag SRE to redeploy that node's model binary. I'll also push a quick guard in the batcher to reject mixed-dim join attempts (fail-fast before coalescing).

maya: Agreed, file a ticket to redeploy node and add a temporary config: `batcher.reject_on_dim_mismatch=true` so we don't coalesce anything that could mismatch.

lucy: Filed ticket SRE-4219 and applied reject_on_dim_mismatch on the route. Customer reports normal now. Will monitor next 24h and schedule a proactive node sweep.

samir: Nice work. Postmortem next steps: confirm root cause (stale model binary vs. mutation in variant mapping), add unit tests for coalesce path, add e2e test for mixed small/large workloads. Assigning @kevin for the guard patch and @maya for infra redeploy coordination.

kevin: Taking the guard patch. I'll open a PR and include a toggled rollout. Quick pseudo for guard:

```go
if batch.has_mixed_output_dims() {
  if cfg.reject_on_dim_mismatch { return HTTP_400("dim mismatch in coalesce") }
  else log.Warn("mixed dims in batch")
}
```

lucy: Thanks all — closing this thread once SRE confirms redeploy. :thumbsup:
